title: Pendulum, 80 cm

source.credit: Rendered by Ansatz with known physics (a school practical: true length 0.80 m, g = 9.81 m/s²)

reference.basis: plain white sheet is standard A4 long side in plane of motion

slow_motion.evidence: no on-screen text or visual cue of slow motion

subjects.description: small orange spherical bob hanging from a string

observation.what_happens: An orange ball suspended by a string swings side to side beneath a fixed mount. It moves from right of centre toward the left and back, continuing to oscillate for the whole clip.

calibration.note: white paper = 0.297 m (plain white sheet is standard A4 long side in plane of motion) spans 146 px in SAM's mask

given: scale: white paper = 0.297 m (plain white sheet is standard A4 long side in plane of motion) spans 146 px in SAM's mask, known to ±6%
pendulum length L = 0.791 m, measured from the radius of the swing with the ruler: hold L fixed and measure g
reasoning: Path fits a circle of radius 0.791 m with 10 deg amplitude and period near 1.8 s, decaying only a few percent over 5.2 s, so it is a nearly ideal pendulum with weak air loss. Candidates test small-angle vs exact sine restoring force and no loss vs linear viscous vs quadratic aerodynamic damping, all with L fixed at 0.791 m to measure g.

caveats: Gravity value inherits the scale uncertainty from the paper reference.
String length was held fixed from a separate measurement, so any error in length shifts gravity.
critique.finding: The ball swings like a textbook pendulum pulling with gravity {g} on a string {L} long. It loses just a tiny bit of swing to friction {gamma} each second.
critique.headline: Swinging ball loses energy slowly to gentle air drag
critique.why_it_won: The linear damping law keeps the swing shrinking steadily while quadratic drag gets too weak when the swing slows.

headline: Swinging ball loses energy slowly to gentle air drag
finding: The ball swings like a textbook pendulum pulling with gravity 9.7 ± 0.58 m/s² on a string 0.791 m long. It loses just a tiny bit of swing to friction 0.0297 ± 0.00041 1/s each second.

eyeball.confidence: medium-low: L from A4 scale ~5% and T from frame counting ~2% dominate; damping envelope barely decays in 8 s so gamma weakly constrained
eyeball.law_in_words: small-angle pendulum theta_ddot + gamma theta_dot + (g/L) theta = 0, period T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g), amplitude envelope ~ exp(-gamma t/2). L obtained by comparing string pivot-to-bob pixels to white paper long side 0.297 m, T obtained by counting frames at 37.5 fps between same-phase crossings, then g = 4 pi^2 L / T^2 and gamma from log decrement of swing amplitude.
